# JVM capability probe

Run this on the **browser JVM kernel** to see which low-level JVM features CheerpJ actually implements. This matters because [dtype-next](https://github.com/cnuernber/dtype-next) — the foundation under tech.ml.dataset → tablecloth → [noj](https://scicloj.github.io/noj/) — leans on exactly these features for its buffer machinery:

- **on-heap primitive arrays** — dtype-next's default containers; if these work, a lot works
- **DirectByteBuffer / off-heap** — `tech.v3.datatype.native-buffer`
- **sun.misc.Unsafe** — raw off-heap reads/writes on hot paths
- **mmap** — how TMD reads Arrow/Parquet without copying
- **threads** — parallel reductions
- **runtime bytecode generation** — how Clojure itself (and dtype-next's `insn` usage) makes code fast

Run all, then compare against a local JVM (`?kernel=server`).

(defn probe [check f]
  (try {:check check :status "ok" :detail (str (f))}
       (catch Throwable t
         {:check check :status "FAIL" :detail (str (class t) ": " (ex-message t))})))

(kind/table
 [(probe "on-heap double[] (1e6 write+sum)"
         #(let [a (double-array 1000000)]
            (dotimes [i 1000000] (aset a i (double i)))
            (areduce a i s 0.0 (+ s (aget a i)))))
  (probe "DirectByteBuffer (allocateDirect)"
         #(let [b (java.nio.ByteBuffer/allocateDirect 64)]
            (.putDouble b 0 42.0)
            (.getDouble b 0)))
  (probe "sun.misc.Unsafe off-heap alloc/read/write"
         #(let [f (.getDeclaredField sun.misc.Unsafe "theUnsafe")
                _ (.setAccessible f true)
                u (.get f nil)
                a (.allocateMemory u 64)]
            (try (.putLong u a 123456)
                 (.getLong u a)
                 (finally (.freeMemory u a)))))
  (probe "mmap (FileChannel/map)"
         #(let [f (java.io.File/createTempFile "probe" ".bin")
                raf (java.io.RandomAccessFile. f "rw")
                ch (.getChannel raf)]
            (try (let [mb (.map ch java.nio.channels.FileChannel$MapMode/READ_WRITE 0 64)]
                   (.putInt mb 0 7)
                   (.getInt mb 0))
                 (finally (.close ch) (.delete f)))))
  (probe "threads (future + deref)"
         #(deref (future (reduce + (range 1000))) 10000 :timeout))
  (probe "pmap (thread pool)"
         #(vec (pmap inc (range 8))))
  (probe "runtime bytecode (eval defrecord)"
         #(do (eval '(defrecord ProbePoint [x y]))
              (str (eval '(->ProbePoint 1 2)))))
  (probe "proxy (runtime subclass)"
         #(str (proxy [java.util.ArrayList] [] (toString [] "proxied!"))))
  (probe "reflection"
         #(count (.getMethods (class {}))))])

## Reading the results

- If **on-heap arrays + threads + runtime bytecode** pass, the pure-JVM core of dtype-next has what it needs; tablecloth-style work on heap-backed columns is plausible.
- If **Unsafe / DirectByteBuffer / mmap** fail, `native-buffer`-backed paths (Arrow, Parquet, mmap'd CSV) won't work as-is — datasets would need to stay on-heap and files load through streams instead of mmap.
- Native/JNI-backed deps are a separate cliff regardless (they'd need recompiling to WASM against CheerpJ's JNI).

See `docs/dtype-next.md` in the repo for the full analysis.
